summary: Shows how far a task has gone: a linear bar in layouts, a circular ring in compact spots. Indeterminate when the duration is unknown.
whenToUse: Tasks that take more than about two seconds and report progress: publishing, importing from Figma, running contrast checks.
Indeterminate (value null) when the task runs but its length is unknown.
Switch tone to success or danger when the task ends, and say so in the label.
whenNotToUse: Short waits or busy controls: use Spinner (or Button loading).
Content that is loading into a layout: use Skeleton in the shape of the content.
A static measurement like storage used or a score: that is a meter, not progress.

dos.title: Label the task, show the value
dos.text: "Publishing tokens 64%" tells users what is happening and how long is left.

dos.title: Use counts when they mean more than percent
dos.text: getAriaValueText and the label can say "12 of 40 pairs".

donts.title: A progress bar that never moves
donts.text: If you cannot report progress, use the indeterminate state rather than a fake value.

accessibility: Base UI Progress: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax; indeterminate drops aria-valuenow.
Needs a name: the label prop, or aria-label when there is no visible label (rings).
The visible value text is aria-hidden; screen readers get it from aria-valuetext (customize with getAriaValueText).
The fill uses the signal color with at least 3:1 against the track and surfaces.
Under reduced motion the indeterminate bar stops sliding and shows a full, softened track instead.
contentGuidelines: Labels use the present participle of the action: "Publishing tokens", "Importing variables".
When done, change the label to the outcome: "Published".
